[BugFix][MoE] Fix MegaMoe prefill buffer sizing (#14439)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

CANN MegaMoe allocates its symmetric communication buffer once from the
MC2 token capacity. When `enable_prefill_mc2` is disabled, that capacity
was derived from the decode graph capture size even though eager prefill
could still select MegaMoe through fused MC2. A larger prefill batch
could therefore exceed the allocated capacity and produce invalid
outputs.

This PR:

- Sizes the MegaMoe buffer from `max_num_batched_tokens` when MegaMoe is
actually eligible.
- Centralizes MegaMoe eligibility in `use_cann_megamoe` so communication
selection, buffer sizing, DP token handling, and BF16/W4A8/W8A8 weight
preparation use the same decision, while preserving the
`dispatch_ffn_combine` fallback.
- Keeps DP token counts uniform for MegaMoe, without disabling the
uneven-token optimization for `dispatch_ffn_combine`.
- Raises an explicit error if a MegaMoe input exceeds the allocated
per-rank capacity.

Fixes #14273.

Related release-branch PR: #14358.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. MegaMoe now allocates enough symmetric-buffer capacity for eager
prefill batches when prefill MC2 is disabled. Non-MegaMoe configurations
continue to use their existing communication path, and an invalid
capacity is reported explicitly instead of producing incorrect output.

### How was this patch tested?

- `git diff --check`
- `python3 -m py_compile vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py
vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py
vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py
vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w4a8.py
vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w8a8_dynamic.py vllm_ascend/utils.py`
- `ruff check vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py
vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py
vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py
vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w4a8.py
vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w8a8_dynamic.py vllm_ascend/utils.py`
- The underlying buffer-sizing fix was validated end-to-end with
DeepSeek V4 W8A8 inference on Ascend A3 using eager prefill, fused MC2
enabled, and prefill MC2 disabled. A prefill batch larger than the
decode graph capture capacity completed without non-finite output and
produced the expected response. This final main-branch adaptation was
verified with the static checks above and was not rerun end-to-end.

No unit test was added because the failure depends on CANN MegaMoe
symmetric-buffer allocation and collective execution across an NPU
communication group.

[Feature][MRV2] Support Eagle3 and DSpark with PP (#14822)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR extends the existing Model Runner V2 speculative-decoding
pipeline-parallel path to support:

- MiniMax M3 with EAGLE3 + PP
- DeepSeek V4 with DSpark + PP

The implementation reuses the existing MRV2 `PPHandler`, request-state
update, and sampled/draft-token broadcast flow. It adds only the model
data and loader handling required by these methods:

- a typed PP transport utility for auxiliary hidden states;
- ordered auxiliary-hidden-state propagation across PP stages;
- receive-buffer construction for transported auxiliary tensors;
- complete local draft-model initialization on the last PP stage with
draft `pipeline_parallel_size=1`;
- EAGLE-specific draft config isolation: EP and EPLB are disabled for
the dense EAGLE draft, while other speculative methods retain the target
configuration;
- DSpark loading support for target quantization inheritance and a local
draft embedding when the target embedding is absent on the last PP
stage.

The EAGLE3 guard is bypassed only for the registered MiniMax M3
architectures, and DSpark PP is enabled only for
`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`. Existing MTP and non-PP paths remain unchanged.

PIECEWISE graph mode is outside the scope of this PR. Eager mode is
covered by the E2E test in this PR. MiniMax M3 was also manually
validated with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`; the unrelated ACLGraph
backend-selection fix needed by that mode is tracked separately in
#15405.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Model Runner V2 users can combine pipeline parallelism with MiniMax
M3 EAGLE3 and DeepSeek V4 DSpark in the supported configurations above.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added an eight-card E2E accuracy test for DeepSeek V4 W8A8, DSpark,
PP2/TP4/EP, eager mode, chunked prefill, and 5 draft tokens.
- Real-weight curl smoke tests completed with coherent deterministic
output and repeated requests without hangs.
- `python3 -m py_compile` on changed Python files.
- `git diff --check`.

#### Manual GPQA-Diamond accuracy

AISBench evaluation used all 198 GPQA-Diamond samples (`b1ed2c`) with a
100% answer extraction rate.

| Model and speculative method | Parallelism | Execution mode | Accuracy
|
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| MiniMax M3 W8A8 + EAGLE3 | PP2 / TP8 / EP | Target `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`,
draft eager | 92.42% |
| DeepSeek V4 W8A8 + DSpark | TP8 / PP1 / EP (pure TP) | Eager | 85.35%
(169/198) |
| DeepSeek V4 W8A8 + DSpark | PP2 / TP4 / EP | Eager | 83.84% (166/198)
|

The DeepSeek V4 pure-TP baseline combines two shards: 85.00% on 100
samples and 85.71% on 98 samples. The PP result combines 85.00% on 100
samples and 82.65% on 98 samples. The two configurations differ by only
three correct answers over the full 198-sample set, so no material
accuracy regression was observed. This PR extends PP transport and draft
initialization without changing target/draft model computation or
verification semantics, and does not affect model accuracy in the
supported modes.

[Doc] Add Triton operator descriptions for l2norm, rope, rope_siso and min_p (#15135)

## Why

Most Triton kernels under `vllm_ascend` have no operator-level
description, so their layout assumptions, constraints and the reason
they diverge from the upstream vLLM kernel are only discoverable by
reading the kernel source.

## What

Add operator docs under `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs`, each with the
same structure (Description / Parameters / Constraints / Origin and
Differences / Test Cases):

- `l2norm.md` — `l2norm_fwd_kernel2_loop`
(`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/fla/l2norm.py`), the forward-only L2
normalization used by the FLA chunked gated delta rule path.
- `rope.md` — `_triton_rope` (`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/rope.py`),
in-place RoPE on the Q/K pair, backing `rope_forward_oot`.
- `rope_siso.md` — `_triton_rope_siso`
(`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/rope.py`), the single-input single-output RoPE
variant used by the SFA lightweight index path.
- `min_p.md` — `_min_p_kernel`
(`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/min_p.py`), min-p sampling filtering,
patched over the upstream `states.apply_min_p`.

Documentation only; no source or test file is modified.

## Notes

- `min_p.md` documents a kernel that lives outside
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton` (`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/sample/min_p.py`). The
doc is still placed under `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs` so all Triton
operator docs stay in one place, with the real source path stated at the
top of the file.
- Each doc's Test Cases section points at the existing accuracy test
under `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton` and
records the precision tolerance actually used, together with the
operator type it follows (reduction / element-wise fp32 accumulation /
exact mask comparison).
- Two behaviours observed while documenting are recorded as constraints
rather than changed here:
- `rope_forward_triton_siso` computes `pad_rope_dim` before the
`rope_dim == -1` inference, so callers must pass an explicit `rope_dim`
(`rope_forward_triton` does not have this ordering issue).
- `_min_p_kernel` skips rows whose `min_p == 0.0` without writing them,
which is only correct because `apply_min_p` passes the same tensor as
input and output.

[Doc][Ops] Add the lightning_attn operator doc (#15051)

## Why

The four Triton kernels of
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/mamba/lightning_attn.py` —
`_fwd_diag_kernel`, `_fwd_kv_parallel`, `_fwd_kv_reduce`,
`_fwd_none_diag_kernel` —
have no spec of any kind: no formula, no parameter list, no record of
the
constraints a caller has to respect. Reading the four of them together
is
currently the only way to find out what the operator computes.

## What

Adds `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/lightning_attn.md`. One document for
all four
kernels, because they have no individual dispatch site — they only ever
run as one
pipeline inside `_attention.forward`.

Contents:

- **Description**: what the operator computes, the closed-form formula
of the tiled
algorithm (intra-block and cross-block terms, and the KV state update),
a
step-by-step table of what each kernel contributes, the dispatch chain
from
`AscendBailingMoELinearAttention` down to the kernels, and the grid
layout of each
  kernel.
- **Parameters**: separate tables for the two Python entry points
(`jit_linear_forward_prefix`, `lightning_attention_npu`) and for each
kernel, with
  `tl.constexpr` versus runtime parameters marked.
- **Constraints**: see the notes below.
- **Test notes**: per kernel, what a case has to check to lock that
kernel down;
  plus what is deliberately not testable today and why.

## Notes

Findings from reading the kernels, **recorded in the doc but not changed
here**, so
the owner can decide whether any deserves its own fix PR:

1. Cross-block token pairs are weighted `exp(-s*(t-j-1))` while pairs
inside one
BLOCK get `exp(-s*(t-j))`. `_fwd_kv_parallel` decays a block state to
the last
token of its block and `_fwd_none_diag_kernel` replays it with
`exp(-s*t_local)`,
so the two paths disagree by `exp(s)` for the same token distance. This
matches
the upstream vLLM / MiniMax GPU implementation, so it is recorded as a
constraint
rather than changed. A consequence worth knowing: segmented prefill is
only
   equivalent to one-shot prefill on a 256-aligned split.
2. `d > 128` is broken: `lightning_attention_npu` chunks `d` by 128 but
hands each
chunk the whole `[b, h, d, e]` `kv_history`, which the kernel then
addresses with
`d = 128`, and it returns the `kv` of the last chunk only. BailingMoE
uses
   `head_dim = 128` and never reaches the path.
3. `block_size` is accepted by both public entry points and silently
ignored;
   `_attention.forward` pins `BLOCK = 256`.

Also recorded: `_attention` has no `backward` despite subclassing
`autograd.Function`; `_fwd_kv_parallel` relies on the masked load alone
where #10276
added a `tl.where` re-mask to `_fwd_diag_kernel`; the returned `kv` is
an *exclusive*
scan, so entry 0 is the incoming history and the final state is the
trailing entry;
and no parameter carries `do_not_specialize` while `b/h/n/d/e` are all
`constexpr`,
so every new shape costs four recompilations.

The test section documents the existing `test_lightning_attn.py` as it
stands — its
13 test functions and 29 cases, its tolerance table, and which kernels
each group of
cases reaches — so the doc and the test file agree. No test change in
this PR.

Note on placement: the doc sits under `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/`,
the same
directory as the other Triton operator docs. Its section layout follows
`csrc/attention/kv_quant_sparse_attn_sharedkv/README.md`, with an extra
`Supported Products` and `Change Log` section.

[Doc] Add apply_penalties Triton operator description (#15087)

## Why

`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/penalty.py` and
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/bincount.py` implement the sampling penalties on
NPU but have no operator description of any kind.

## What

Add `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/apply_penalties.md`, structured as
Description / Parameters / Constraints / Origin and Differences / Test
Cases. The two kernels only ever run as one pipeline behind
`apply_penalties_triton`, so they share a single document. Besides the
formula, dispatch chain, grid layout and parameter table, it records the
constraints found while reading the kernels:

- the padding contract — token ids `>= vocab_size` are ignored, so
callers must pad with `vocab_size` rather than `-1`;
- the `int32 [num_seqs, vocab_size]` intermediate histograms, allocated
once per token tensor;
- `num_seqs == 0` is not a no-op: the histogram helpers return early,
but `_apply_all_penalties_triton` still issues a zero-sized launch, so
callers must skip an empty batch;
- the two initialisation prerequisites for standalone callers:
`init_device_properties_triton()` for `get_vectorcore_num()`, and an
initialised `AscendConfig` for the `enable_reduce_sample` branch in
`bincount.py`;
- the `vocab_start_idx = tp_rank * vocab_size` window, which is the
vllm-ascend-specific difference from the upstream `apply_penalties` this
operator was migrated from (#6979).

commits.message:
[Feature][xlite] Add preliminary support for GLM-5.2 with shared DSA indexer in the xlite backend (#15137)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Extends xlite support for GLM-5.2, which introduce a **shared indexer
topk** scheme where only a subset of layers run a dedicated sparse
indexer while the rest rely on a shared top-k selection. The previous
adapter assumed every layer carried its own indexer weights, which
breaks weight extraction and KV-cache layout for these new models.

The xlite backend was updated to `0.2.0rc1` to adapt for the changes
already.

More specifically,

- `kv cache` registration is now handled per model architecture
- indexer normalization weights and biases are handled in their original
precision (for GLM-5.1, BF16; for GLM-5.2, FP32)
- The `XliteModelRunner` is refactored to better incorporate
`NPUModelRunner` as the fallback implementation and `XliteModelRunner`'s
`XliteWrapper` as the default xlite implementation.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No, not on the API level. However, users must upgrade from
`xlite==0.2.0rc0` to `xlite==0.2.0rc1` per `requirements-dev.txt`.

### How was this patch tested?

We benchmarked model accuracies with `GLM-5.2-w8a8` and `GLM-5.1-w8a8`
using `aisbench`. The
[batch_aisbench.py](https://atomgit.com/openeuler/GVirt/blob/master/xlite/tests/e2e/batch_aisbench.py)
script was used with 416 questions from the `ceval` dataset on one Atlas
A3:

```bash
python batch_aisbench.py "/root/benchmark" \
--num-prompts 8 \
--model-dir "/mnt/sdb/models" \
--models "GLM-5.2-w8a8" "GLM-5.1-w8a8" \
--tps 8 8 \
--dps 2 2 \
--eps 1 1 \
-MNS 64 \
-MML 8192 \
--xlite 2 1 0 \
--broadcast-xlite
```

Each model is exercised across three backends — `xlite full` (prefill +
decode on xlite), `xlite decode-only` (prefill on native aclgraph,
decode on xlite), and `aclgraph` (native baseline).

| Model | Dataset | TP | EP | DP | MTP | Backend | Metric | Accuracy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-5.1-w8a8 | ceval-weighted | 8 | Y | 2 | 0 | xlite full |
weighted_average | 93.19 |
| GLM-5.1-w8a8 | ceval-weighted | 8 | Y | 2 | 0 | xlite decode-only |
weighted_average | 92.72 |
| GLM-5.1-w8a8 | ceval-weighted | 8 | Y | 2 | 0 | aclgraph |
weighted_average | 93.42 |
| GLM-5.2-w8a8 | ceval-weighted | 8 | Y | 2 | 0 | xlite full |
weighted_average | 84.67 |
| GLM-5.2-w8a8 | ceval-weighted | 8 | Y | 2 | 0 | xlite decode-only |
weighted_average | 89.71 |
| GLM-5.2-w8a8 | ceval-weighted | 8 | Y | 2 | 0 | aclgraph |
weighted_average | 93.19 |

No accuracy degradation observed for `GLM-5.1`. However, for `GLM-5.2`,
the accuracy from the current `xlite` implementation is observably
lower. This is due to a **known indexer top-k accuracy issue** by the
upstream top-k compute bug at
<https://atomgit.com/openeuler/GVirt/issues/27>. The fix is tracked in
the xlite backend and will be picked up via an `xlite` release bump; no
change is expected in this vllm-ascend docking.

commits.message:
[Performance][Spec Decode] Shard DeepSeek V4 DSpark main projection across TP ranks (#15123)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4 DSpark currently implements `main_proj` with
`ReplicatedLinear`, so every tensor-parallel rank stores the full
projection weight and executes the full projection.

This PR replaces it with `ColumnParallelLinear`. The output features are
sharded across TP ranks, and `gather_output=True` restores the full
hidden state before RMSNorm and the downstream draft layers.

For DeepSeek V4 Pro, the BF16 `main_proj` weight has shape `[7168,
21504]`. With TP=8, this change reduces persistent weight memory on each
rank from 294 MiB to 36.75 MiB, saving 257.25 MiB per rank and about
2.01 GiB across the TP group, excluding temporary communication buffers.

It also reduces the projection weight read on each rank to one eighth of
the replicated implementation. This is expected to provide a significant
memory-access benefit during decode, where the small-M projection is
more bandwidth-sensitive. Decode end-to-end performance has not been
quantified yet.

Performance profiling on DeepSeek V4 Pro:

| Configuration | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TP=8, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` | 9 ms | 2 ms |

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This only changes the internal tensor-parallel execution strategy of
the DSpark main projection.

### How was this patch tested?

- Profiled DeepSeek V4 Pro with TP=8 and `--max-num-batched-tokens
8192`; `main_proj` latency decreased from 9 ms to 2 ms.
- `python3 -m py_compile vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v4/dspark.py`
- `git diff --check github/main...HEAD`

No new unit test was added because the change uses the existing
`ColumnParallelLinear` output sharding and AllGather path without
introducing a new operator or interface.

[Feature] Optimize MLA prolog by sharing quantization results + remove redundant stream syncsMla prolog multistream overlap (#12883)

## Summary

Optimize `AscendDSAImpl._mla_prolog_multistream()` with two changes that
reduce duplicate work and increase dual-stream parallelism:

1. **Share quantized hidden_states** between wq_a and wkv when their
   quantization schemes are identical and communication status matches.
   Saves one `npu_dynamic_quant` call (full-tensor read + per-row absmax
   reduction) on W8A8, and one kernel launch on W4A8 or TP paths.

2. **Remove redundant `wait_stream(aux)`** at Part1→Part2 and
Part2→Part3
boundaries. The Q projection chain does not depend on any intermediate
   KV results; these syncs only narrow the parallel window between the
   main-stream Q path and aux-stream KV path.

## Motivation

In the 3-block multi-stream scheduling of MLA prolog
(Part1/Part2/Part3),
the Q chain (wq_a → q_norm → wq_b → q_rms → rope) and KV chain (wkv →
kv_norm → rope → scatter) are dispatched to main/aux NPU streams
respectively to overlap Vector and Cube unit utilization.

Two inefficiencies were identified:

- **Duplicate quantization**: Both `cv_wq_a.quantize(hidden_states)` and
  `cv_wkv.quantize(hidden_states)` read the same input and produce the
  same output when quantization types match. For W8A8 this means two
  full-tensor reads + absmax reductions; for W4A8/TP this means two
  redundant kernel launches + event synchronization overhead.

- **Unnecessary stream syncs**: The `wait_stream(aux)` at the end of
  Part1 and Part2 block the main stream until aux completes its KV work,
  but the main stream's subsequent Q operations never read KV
  intermediates. Only the tail `wait_stream(aux)` before q_rms+rope is
  necessary (to ensure KV cache is fully written before attention reads
  it).

## Changes

### `vllm-ascend/vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py`

- `_mla_prolog_multistream()` Part1: Add `share_quant` detection using
  `type(wq_a._quant_method) is type(wkv._quant_method)` (exact type
  match) plus `_has_communication` status equality. When true, call
  `quantize()` once and alias the result for both Q and KV paths.
  Falls back to original dual-quant path when quant types differ.

- Remove `main_stream.wait_stream(aux_stream)` after Part1 and Part2.
  Keep the tail `wait_stream(aux)` which is the sole hard dependency
  (KV scatter must complete before attention reads swa_kv_cache).

[Feature][Model] Support GLM-5.3 native FP8 checkpoints on Ascend 950 (#15346)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds support for
[GLM-5.3](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/ZhipuAI/GLM-5.3) on Ascend
950 products.

GLM-5.3 is the first GLM release published with block-wise FP8 weights
instead of BF16, so it is served through the native FP8 path
(`AscendFp8Config`) rather than through a ModelSlim-quantized
checkpoint. That path had not been exercised by a merged-projection
model before, and four issues surfaced. Each is independent of GLM-5.3
itself and affects any native FP8 checkpoint with the same shape.

**1. Block-wise scales of merged projections lost their last row.**

`AscendFp8BlockLinearMethod.get_pergroup_param` declared
`weight_scale_inv` with `packed_dim`/`packed_factor`. That mechanism
exists for bit packing, where a shard is always a whole number of packs,
so vLLM converts shard bounds to scale entries with a plain division.

Block sizes carry no such guarantee. GLM-5.3 merges a 2048-row
`q_a_proj` with a 576-row `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` into `fused_qkv_a_proj`,
and `576 / 128` is 4.5. The loader wrote 4 scale rows where 5 were
needed, so row 20 of every `fused_qkv_a_proj` scale in all 78 layers
stayed at its allocation-time contents. The kv half of attention was
scaled by zero from layer 0 onward and the model emitted pure noise.

The fix registers the scale as `BlockQuantScaleParameter`, the type vLLM
already rounds up for at every loader site
(`MergedColumnParallelLinear`, `ColumnParallelLinear`,
`QKVParallelLinear`, `RowParallelLinear`), and exposes
`weight_block_size` on the layer for `adjust_block_scale_shard` to read.

**2. MXFP8 requantization produced a scale in the wrong layout.**

On Ascend 950 the resolved weights are requantized to MXFP8.
`npu_dynamic_mx_quant` returns the scale with its group axis split in
two (`[N, G/2, 2]`), while both MXFP8 schemes consume `[N, G]`. This
raised `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` in
`w8a8_mxfp8.py`. Verified numerically on device: flattening the trailing
axis reproduces the input at 0.0235 relative error, whereas transposing
first gives 0.1930.

**3. `kv_b_proj` was requantized even though SFA needs it dense.**

SFA splits `kv_b_proj` into `W_UK`/`W_UV` and disposes of the layer, so
it never runs a matmul. GLM-5.3's `modules_to_not_convert` does not
exclude it, so it was requantized to MXFP8 and SFA hit `assert
isinstance(self.kv_b_proj.quant_method, UnquantizedLinearMethod)`. The
layer is now skipped, and the SFA assertion checks the weight dtype
instead of the quant method class, since a scheme can own a layer
without quantizing it.

**4. MTP acceptance rate was pinned at exactly 0%.**

`_maybe_share_lm_head` decides whether the MTP draft reuses the target
`lm_head` by comparing weights. That works for DeepSeek, which ships a
`shared_head.head` identical to `lm_head`. GLM-5.3 ships no MTP head at
all, so `shared_head.head` held its allocation-time contents, compared
unequal, and the draft computed logits from uninitialized memory. Every
drafted token was rejected.

The information needed was already available:
`AscendDeepSeekMTP._maybe_set_own_lm_head` inspects `loaded_weights` for
exactly this. It now also records the negative case, and
`_maybe_share_lm_head` asks the model before falling back to the weight
comparison, which is kept so checkpoints shipping an identical head
still deduplicate it.

**Unrelated startup fix.** `sparse_kv_offload_manager` suppressed only
`ImportError` around its optional `memfabric_hybrid` import. That
package provisions an AICPU kernel on import and raises its own
`ProvisioningError` when the CANN build toolchain is incomplete, which
aborted worker startup for an opt-in feature.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. GLM-5.3 can be served on Ascend 950 products. No documentation is
added: GLM-5.3 is architecturally identical to GLM-5.2, so the existing
GLM-5.2 guide already covers its deployment.

Two limitations are documented rather than fixed:

- **Expert parallel is unavailable on this platform.**
`--enable-expert-parallel` forces the MC2 path on A5, and MC2 cannot
acquire HCCL communication resources on an Atlas 350 topology
(`mc2_context.cpp:158 GetHcclCommLink: No matching communication
protocol found in HCCL links protocol is 6`). This is an interconnect
capability, not something the plugin can work around.
- **Speculative decoding runs the draft eagerly**, as for the rest of
the GLM series.

No behavior changes for other models. The `packed_dim`/`packed_factor`
path is untouched for the schemes that use it, and the weight-comparison
branch of `_maybe_share_lm_head` is preserved.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests** (`pytest -q
tests/ut/quantization/methods/test_fp8_block.py
tests/ut/quantization/test_method_adapters.py
tests/ut/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer.py`, 58 passed). New cases
cover each fix:

- `test_block_quant_scale_uses_the_upstream_parameter_type` builds the
exact GLM-5.3 merge (`output_partition_sizes=[2048, 576]`, block 128)
and asserts the parameter type and `weight_block_size`.
- `test_pergroup_param_declares_block_scale_and_loader_hints` asserts
the bit-packing hints stay absent.
- `test_requantizes_to_mxfp8_on_950` and
`test_requantizes_every_expert_on_950` feed the split layout the
operator really emits and assert the flattened result.
- `test_kv_b_proj_is_left_dense_for_the_attention_backend`.
- `TestMtpSharesTheTargetLmHead` covers all three cases: no head
shipped, a head the draft owns, and an identical head that should still
be deduplicated.

mode, no local patches outside this PR:

export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

The single-request figure is one chat completion measured end to end:
2465 total tokens in 69.307 s.

The concurrent figures come from:

```shell
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model /data/GLM-5.3 --tokenizer /data/GLM-5.3 --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 64000 --random-output-len 3000 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts 10 --request-rate inf \
  --temperature 0 --ignore-eos --served-model-name glm-53 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

Two caveats on reading those numbers. TTFT is dominated by queueing
rather than prefill cost: `--request-rate inf` submits all ten 64K
prompts at once against `--max-num-seqs 16`, so later requests wait
through earlier prefills. And the 98.90% acceptance rate reflects the
random-token dataset with `--ignore-eos`, on which generation
degenerates into highly predictable output; the 89.9% measured on a
natural-language prompt is the more representative figure.

No e2e accuracy config is added: there is no measured accuracy baseline
for GLM-5.3 yet, and a guessed threshold would be worse than none. Happy
to add one once a baseline exists.
